E014 — Individual-waveform repeatability

Image edition. Choose a participant and waveform; both stay separate, as do first and second presentations. All 62 electrodes and all ten feature representations are available. The page displays pre-rendered images and small summary tables. It does not download EEG epochs or numerical map arrays.

Methods, interpretation and image resolution

Ten participants, 595 complete pairs, 1,190 events; simple 0.5–30 Hz filtering, average reference and [-250,-50)-ms baseline. No ICA refit, new exclusions, classifier, peak selection or latency alignment. The original 14-channel results reproduce the preserved E011 reference.

Waveform-specific deviations use half-specific adjustment for comparison context, elapsed time and presentation position. Total responses retain observed comparison-cell means. A repeatable total response need not distinguish waveform identity or have neural origin.

Voltage and first/second derivatives retain 1/5/25/50/100/200-ms bins; derivatives use the fixed 25-ms local estimator. 1-ms spacing does not imply independent physiological resolution. Images have fixed pixel resolution; this affects display only, not the estimates or reported correlations. Palette colors are discretized for rendering. WebP compression is lossless for the rendered pixels. The full-precision numerical report is retained locally.

Alpha/beta use eleven overlapping 500-ms Hann total-power windows with a 50-ms step and 2-Hz Fourier spacing. Their plotted centres are 300–800 ms; each marker summarizes a 500-ms window, not 50-ms independent activity. These are filtered total-power features, not induced power.

xDAWN fits only independent calibration pairs (two components per waveform, regularization 0.1). Both A/B halves are held out. Matched 62- and 14-sensor controls share the same held-out trials and calibration-only RMS normalization. Joint shape r removes each feature's temporal mean. Compare these three matched views to one another. Learned component names denote class/rank slots, not fixed electrodes or anatomical sources.

Channel-quality flags are descriptive and remove no channels or pairs. Absence of a flag does not establish neural origin. Separate participant/waveform patterns remain primary; this edition adds no group averaging, corrected feature discovery or decoding result.
